name: Pipe Racks — Steel and Piping Interface

activities: install shoes, guides, anchors, rigid/spring supports on rack beams
set largest/lowest-tier lines first for crane access
cable tray and electrical/instrument tray on dedicated tiers
field welding and NDT of rack piping
hydrotest of rack lines by test package
connect rack headers to ISBL/OSBL units

typical_relationships.reason: columns are set on cured foundations with grouted base plates

typical_relationships.before: erect, survey and bolt-up rack steel
typical_relationships.after: install any piping or cable tray on the rack
typical_relationships.reason: the load path and safe access depend on the steel being complete and released

typical_relationships.after: install small-bore / upper-tier lines and tray
typical_relationships.reason: upper-tier work blocks crane access to the lower/larger lines, so they go in first

typical_relationships.before: install pipe supports on the rack
typical_relationships.reason: the pipe lands on its supports

typical_relationships.after: impose heavy pipe load on it
typical_relationships.reason: PFP and grout are done before the steel is fully loaded and access is lost

typical_relationships.before: coordinate cable-tray tier with piping tier
typical_relationships.reason: tray and pipe share rack tiers and must be sequenced to avoid rework
the header is proven before it is connected and put in service

interfaces.requirement: rack is steel — foundation, erection, survey and bolt-up gate all rack MEP work
foundations, anchor bolts and grouting complete before steel erection
cable tray and cables share rack tiers with piping — coordinated to avoid clash
power/tray tiers routed on the rack alongside piping
rack carries the headers routed between units; header route ready before tie-ins
rack carries utility mains between units
passive fire protection on rack steel; insulation on rack lines after test

testing_requirements: Steel: connection torque/bolt-up inspection, field-connection weld inspection, survey/plumb and elevation checks
Rack piping: same weld NDT and hydrotest regime as its service class
commissioning_dependencies: Rack structurally complete and released before line commissioning of its headers
Headers on the rack tested and flushed before feeding connected systems
typical_exceptions: Modular / pre-assembled rack units (PAR/PAU) delivered with piping and tray pre-installed — the field sequence collapses into module-yard fabrication then set-in-place
Grade-level sleeper-supported racks skip steel erection — foundations/sleepers only
evidence: Pipe-rack steel was founded, erected, surveyed and bolted-up — and fireproofed where required — before any piping or cable tray was installed, and the lowest/largest-bore lines went in first because upper-tier work blocks crane access to them.
